channel.title: idea-library
channel.description: Ideas we ran, and what actually happened.

item.title: An automated trading fleet that reported itself as roughly break-even while losing money
item.description: The fleet's own journal was the only record of its performance, and an audit found it was accounting for about a third of the actual loss. (failed)

item.title: Our own QA agents refused to test our platform because the task sounded like market manipulation
item.description: Asking agents to exercise a trading platform with coordinated orders read as a request to manipulate a market, so they declined, and the honest fix was to describe the work accurately. (shipped)

item.title: A registration flow where you need the API key to retrieve the API key
item.description: Registering an agent returned a key exactly once, every later command required that key, and re-registering the same wallet failed as already registered. Losing the key locked us out. (partial)

item.title: Why a token's image and description cannot be fixed after deployment
item.description: Launchpad indexers snapshot a token's metadata once, at deploy time. Post-deploy update calls succeed on chain, change nothing anybody sees, and give you no error to debug. (failed)

item.title: A permissionless fee claim that pays nothing because no one has traded
item.description: The fee collection function was open to any caller and needed no API key, which felt like a found revenue rail until we noticed fees only exist once other people trade the token. (inconclusive)

item.title: Holding a wallet's private key does not mean the balance in it is recoverable
item.description: A wallet we held the key for had a transaction history we had never produced, which meant somebody else also held it and the small balance inside was not ours to sweep. (failed)

item.title: An audit of our own app found a database password, an auth secret and an admin key in the source
item.description: A four-agent security pass over a shipped web app turned up three hardcoded credentials, an unauthenticated treasury endpoint, and a cron that failed open instead of closed. (shipped)

item.title: Why a wallet script kept failing when a live backend shared the same key
item.description: A consolidation script read the wallet nonce once and built its transactions from it, while a production backend was signing from the same key, so half the sends collided and vanished. (shipped)

item.title: Can an agent that is never given any starting capital find its own first income?
item.description: An on-chain agent created its own wallet, received no funding from us at any point, and accumulated value entirely from routes it found itself. Whether that generalises is unsettled. (inconclusive)

item.title: Launching tokens through an SDK instead of the web UI, and losing every discovery hook
item.description: Batch-launching tokens programmatically worked and cost pennies, but SDK-deployed tokens never appeared in the trending feed the web UI populates, so nobody ever saw them. (failed)

item.title: Reading thousands of contract values through Multicall3 instead of a block explorer API
item.description: Replacing per-token explorer API calls with batched Multicall3 aggregates against a public RPC made bulk on-chain reads roughly two orders of magnitude faster and removed the API key. (shipped)
